hints.title: Triangular Level Collapse Obstacle
hints.text: Moving from the apex to the base of a triangle permits stepping to adjacent indices on the tier below. How can calculating minimum costs upward from the base eliminate choices at each stage?

hints.title: Bottom-Up Triangular Reduction Invariant
hints.text: The minimum path sum starting at element (r, c) equals triangle[r][c] plus the minimum of the optimal sub-paths starting at (r + 1, c) and (r + 1, c + 1).

hints.title: In-Place Base Tier Compression Procedure
hints.text: Copy the bottom row of the triangle into a 1D array. Iterate from the second-to-last row up to the top apex: for each position c, update the entry to the current cell value plus the minimum of entry c and entry c + 1. Return the single value at index 0.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of rows in the triangle
complexity.notes: Total elements processed is N * (N + 1) / 2 using a 1D buffer of length N.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Top-down branching without caching checks 2^N paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Bottom-up 1D array consumes O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using bottom-up order to naturally converge to a single apex result without finding the min of the last row.
